Symptoms: Long elliptical tan lesions with wavy margins and water-soaked borders on leaves; lesions coalesce.
Causes: Airborne conidia; favoured by moderate temperature and humid conditions.
Favorable_Weather: Temperature 18–27°C, RH >80%, heavy dew, rainy weather.
Chemical_Treatment: Mancozeb 75 WP, Zineb 75 WP, Propiconazole 25 EC.
Prevention: Grow resistant hybrids; destroy crop residues; avoid late planting.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Spray Mancozeb at first appearance; remove lower diseased leaves.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/L for TLB management.

Symptoms: Small circular to elongated brick-red pustules on both leaf surfaces; yellow chlorotic areas around pustules.
Causes: Airborne urediniospores from alternate host (Oxalis species).
Favorable_Weather: Temperature 16–23°C, high humidity, heavy dew; prevalent in cooler upland areas.
Chemical_Treatment: Propiconazole 25 EC, Mancozeb 75 WP.
Prevention: Grow rust-resistant hybrids; early planting; avoid susceptible varieties in high-risk areas.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Spray Propiconazole at first pustule appearance.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends propiconazole-based fungicides for maize rust control.

Symptoms: Rectangular tan-grey lesions between leaf veins; lesions enlarge and coalesce; premature leaf death.
Causes: Airborne and residue-borne conidia; conservation tillage increases risk.
Favorable_Weather: Temperature 25–30°C, RH >90%, extended leaf wetness periods, poor air circulation.
Organic_Treatment: Neem oil 2%; Trichoderma harzianum soil application.
Chemical_Treatment: Propiconazole 25 EC, Azoxystrobin 23 SC, Tebuconazole 25 WG.
Prevention: Grow resistant hybrids; crop rotation; remove crop residues after harvest.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Spray Propiconazole or Azoxystrobin at disease onset.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends propiconazole-based fungicides for gray leaf spot control.

Symptoms: Dark brown target-board concentric ring lesions on older leaves; yellow halo; defoliation; stem canker.
Causes: Airborne and seed-borne Alternaria conidia; debris-borne.
Favorable_Weather: Temperature 24–29°C, high humidity, alternating wet/dry periods, wounded plants.
Organic_Treatment: Neem oil 2%; Copper sulphate 1% spray; Trichoderma seed treatment.
Chemical_Treatment: Mancozeb 75 WP, Chlorothalonil 75 WP, Azoxystrobin 23 SC.
Prevention: Use certified disease-free seed; crop rotation; remove crop debris; stake plants for air circulation.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Remove lower infected leaves; spray Mancozeb immediately; improve drainage.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/L at 7-day intervals for early blight.

Symptoms: Irregular water-soaked dark brown patches on leaves; white sporulation on underside; rapid browning and collapse.
Causes: Airborne sporangia; water-borne zoospores; highly destructive oomycete.
Favorable_Weather: Temperature 10–25°C, RH >90%, cool moist weather, foggy conditions.
Organic_Treatment: Copper sulphate 1% spray; remove infected plants; biocontrol with Bacillus subtilis.
Chemical_Treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 72 WP, Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP, Dimethomorph 50 WP.
Prevention: Grow resistant varieties; avoid overhead irrigation; improve air circulation.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Remove and destroy infected plants; spray Metalaxyl immediately; stop overhead irrigation.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 72 WP @ 2.5 g/L for late blight control.

Scientific_Name: Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV)
Symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of leaves; vein thickening; plant stunting; reduced fruiting.
Causes: Transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); no mechanical transmission.
Favorable_Weather: Hot dry weather (30–38°C) favoring whitefly; late season planting.
Organic_Treatment: Yellow sticky traps; neem oil 2% spray for whitefly control; silver reflective mulch.
Chemical_Treatment: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL, Thiamethoxam 25 WG for whitefly vector control.
Prevention: Use virus-tolerant varieties (Arka Rakshak, Pusa Rohini); control whitefly; rogue infected plants.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Remove infected plants; spray systemic insecticide for whitefly; use reflective mulch.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends whitefly management and virus-tolerant tomato varieties.

Symptoms: Sudden wilting of entire plant; plant recovers at night; brown slimy ooze from cut stem in water.
Causes: Soil-borne bacteria; enters through roots; spreads via irrigation water.
Favorable_Weather: Temperature 28–35°C; high soil moisture; sandy loam soils.
Organic_Treatment: Soil solarization 30–40 days; application of lime; Pseudomonas fluorescens biocontrol.
Chemical_Treatment: Copper oxychloride 50 WP drench, Streptomycin + Tetracycline.
Prevention: Soil solarization; crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops; use resistant rootstocks.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Remove and destroy wilted plants; soil drench with Copper oxychloride; avoid reinfection.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends soil solarization and Pseudomonas fluorescens for bacterial wilt management.

Symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with white/grey centres and dark brown borders on lower leaves; defoliation.
Causes: Fungal; rain-splashed spores; crop debris; seed-borne.
Favorable_Weather: Temperature 20–25°C, RH >90%, rainy conditions, overhead irrigation.
Chemical_Treatment: Mancozeb 75 WP, Chlorothalonil 75 WP, Copper oxychloride 50 WP.
Prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation; stake plants; destroy crop debris; use clean seed.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Remove lower infected leaves; spray Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil for Septoria leaf spot management.

Symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings and yellow halos on leaves; spots on fruit.

Chemical_Treatment: Azoxystrobin 23 SC, Difenoconazole 25 EC.

Immediate_Farmer_Action: Spray Azoxystrobin at first lesion appearance.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends azoxystrobin-based fungicides for target spot in tomato.

Symptoms: Tiny white/yellow stippling on leaves; bronzing; webbing on underside; premature leaf drop.
Causes: Mite infestation; hot dry conditions amplify population; pesticide-induced resurgence.
Organic_Treatment: Neem oil 5% spray; release predatory mite Phytoseiulus persimilis.
Chemical_Treatment: Abamectin 1.9 EC, Spiromesifen 22.9 SC, Propargite 57 EC.
Prevention: Maintain adequate soil moisture; avoid dust; use reflective mulch.
Immediate_Farmer_Action: Spray abamectin on underside of leaves; improve irrigation to reduce drought stress.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR recommends abamectin and neem oil sprays for spider mite control in tomato.

Symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottle on leaves; small misshapen fruit; bitter taste; tree decline.

Immediate_Farmer_Action: Remove infected trees; control psyllid vector with Imidacloprid; replant with certified material.
Govt_ICAR_Recommendation: ICAR-NRC Citrus recommends certified nursery material and psyllid management for HLB prevention.
